messages:
maya: Quick follow-up on FA-v3 rollout — observed unexpected latency regression on short sequences (<=64) after switching from FA-v2 for llama-2-13B on the dedicated pool. Telemetry shows increased allocator churn and GPU memory fragmentation. Anyone else seeing this?

arjun: Yea reproduced on staging. Hypothesis: FA-v3 workspace allocation strategy reserves larger slabs for kernel tiling which leaves more unused fragments on short seqs. Numbers from my run: v2 median=5.2ms (seq64 bs1), v3 median=6.0ms, p95 went from 14ms -> 18ms.

tj: Added more traces — KV cache behavior unchanged. GPU resident memory per worker is up ~+0.8GB with v3. Free-list grows and we see more allocator ops. Suspect workspace alignment and tile rounding.

anika: Could be kernel selection too — runtime may be picking a "mid-seq" fa kernel for mixed-shape batches. We should prefer short-seq kernels when max_seq <= 64. Also consider shape-aware bucketing before dynamic batching.

ben: Proposal: runtime fallback heuristic. If we detect >5% median latency regression for a model+shape combo over a 10s sliding window OR allocator churn > X events/s, fall back to fa_v2 for that combo. Tag combos in telemetry so rollbacks are surgical.

infra-bot: New feature flag suggestion: redwood.runtime.attn_kernel.strategy with values ["shape-first","throughput-first","balanced"]. Default: "balanced". Can be toggled per-deployment.

maya: I'll add telemetry labels first: attn.kernel_chosen, attn.workspace_bytes, attn.alloc_events, attn.shape_bucket. Also want a microbenchmark: 1k requests seq32 bs1 at 80 QPS for 60s to measure median/p95 and memory. Who can run?

arjun: Ran the microbench on r-dedicated-prod-staging: v2 median=3.9ms p95=10.1ms mem=6.2GB; v3 median=4.8ms p95=12.6ms mem=7.0GB. Also saw extra memcpy ops in timeline — likely extra workspace copies for tiling/resizing.

tj: Pseudocode for a stricter kernel selection rule that we can toggle in runtime: 
```
// pick kernel by shape-first policy
if (shape.max_seq <= 64) return kernel_shortseq;
if (batch_size <= 2 && shape.max_seq <= 128) return kernel_shortseq;
if (expected_throughput > THROUGHPUT_THRESH) return kernel_midseq;
return kernel_longseq;
```
This is conservative but should avoid regressing short-seq latency.

anika: Rollout plan: canary 5% traffic for 24h with perf gating. Gating rules: fail if median + p95 delta exceeds 7% or allocator_events/s > threshold. Auto-rollback on failure. Need dashboards and an alert.

perf-bot: Logged experiment: exp/attn/fa3_shortseq_2026-03-18; v3 delta +23% median, +27% p95 for shortseq workload.

maya: Action items: (1) telemetry labels PR (maya) (2) add kernel policy config + default to shape-first for shortseq (arjun) (3) implement runtime fallback + auto-gate (tj) (4) run canary + microbench and collect perf_bench traces (anika). Sync tomorrow 10:00am PT.

ben: Quick Q — does quantized path (int8/bf16 mixed) change workspace sizing? earlier quantized kernels had different workspace footprints.

maya: Yes — quantized kernels allocate different workspace layouts. Add quantization-mode dimension to telemetry and the kernel selection rule.

anika: Also add a small sampling profiler to record memcpy/copy breakdown per request for one in 1000 requests — will help root cause.

tj: I'll draft the rollout gating logic and a feature-flag matrix. If we land shape-first policy, we should be able to flip back quickly if microbench fails.

maya: Thanks everyone. If you see an urgent regression, tag #incidents and ping me. :thumbsup:
